transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Start time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Lena Torres, Evan Chu, Maya Singh, Rajesh Varma, Kira Moore, Ana Gomez, and all Redwood employees (virtual)

Summary (auto): Quick Q1 recap, roadmap highlights for Dedicated and Private, announcement of Redwood Optimize beta, hiring updates, security progress, and open Q&A.

[00:00] Lena Torres: Good morning everyone, welcome to the April all-hands. Uh, quick housekeeping  recording is on, slide deck is in the #all-hands channel, and we'll have Q&A at the end. Thanks for joining across timezones.

[00:28] Lena Torres: Okay first up, Q1 results. Really proud  we hit the top end of the ARR targets, up 18% quarter-over-quarter. Gross margin improved slightly as we rolled out a few batching improvements in the runtime, so thanks to the infra and engineering teams for that work.

[01:05] Evan Chu: Yeah I'll say on infra, the continuous batching change reduced median token cost about 9% in our hosted tier, and the Dedicated beta has been stable in the early customers. There's more perf work coming  kernel selection improvements and better kv cache heuristics.

[01:39] Maya Singh: On product, we shipped the function-calling improvements and structured output hooks which customers are already using for internal automation. The big thing for Q2 is focusing on Dedicated/Private parity  making sure Private installations get the same QC and rollout features as hosted.

[02:12] Rajesh Varma: Ops  we've been prioritizing autoscaling safety, and the next release will include a predictive scaler that learns sequence-length distributions. Early internal benchmarks show latency SLOs hold even under bursty traffic. Notes: more testing needed for edge cases.

[02:49] Kira Moore: From GTM, pipeline looks healthy. A mix of AI-native startups and a couple of enterprise trials  some are explicit about requiring VPC or on-prem. We're pushing contracts and we've got a few prospects evaluating Dedicated for Q3.

[03:20] Lena Torres: Alright, product roadmap specifics. Maya?

[03:25] Maya Singh: Thanks. Roadmap bullets: 1) Dedicated GA improvements: predictable throughput and better autoscale policies; 2) Private deployment: simplified installer and improved KMS integrations; 3) Redwood Optimize: beta will open next week for selected customers  tooling that suggests batching, quantization profiles, and model suggestions based on workload. We'll share signup link after this call.

[04:03] Evan Chu: I want to call out two engineering tradeoffs  latency vs cost. Optimize is designed to help customers pick quantization and batching that stay within their latency SLOs. Also, we're doing runtime kernel selection so we can choose fast paths for popular model families.

[04:35] Audience Voice (unlabeled): quick q about on-prem  will it support air-gapped installs?

[04:41] Maya Singh: Yes, air-gapped packaging is in the roadmap. The Private (on-prem) distribution will include offline installers and an ops runbook. We'll coordinate with security for audits.

[05:03] Lena Torres: Security update  Ana?

[05:07] Ana Gomez: SOC 2 Type II work is on track. We have three controls still in progress related to change management. We're targeting completion by end of June for the Type II report. Also finalizing the security FAQ and we'll publish it to the Trust Center next week. Note: for customers requesting specific evidence, contact security@redwood.com and we'll set up an audit pack.

[05:43] Rajesh Varma: One thing to add, for Private customers we support KMS integrations and HSM via PKCS11 now in beta  if you're on a customer project needing HSM, contact SEs.

[06:02] Kira Moore: On pricing conversations, a common objection is unit economics for high-throughput use cases. Our response has been to run Optimize pilots and propose Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable unit costs.

[06:24] Audience (chat): competitor question  how are we different from Anthropic or OpenAI endpoint products?

[06:30] Lena Torres: Short answer: we focus on inference economics and deployment flexibility. We give customers the runtime controls and observability to hit latency, cost, and reliability targets across hosted, dedicated and private. We'll publish more benchmark examples soon.

[06:55] Maya Singh: Also, our differentiation is rollout tooling (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and token-level cost telemetry, which helps product teams optimize actual unit economics.

[07:20] Lena Torres: Hiring update  we've ramped hiring in SRE, SE, and Sales. New leaders: welcome Rajesh to his expanded role leading infra and runtime, and we've promoted Maya to Head of Product. Congrats to both.

[07:43] Rajesh Varma: Thanks. We're scaling the infra team; priority is to reduce tail latency and improve capacity planning. If you see tickets in our backlog that look like blocking customer work, please flag them.

[08:05] Lena Torres: OK now  spotlight: Redwood Optimize. Maya take us through the user story.

[08:11] Maya Singh: Optimize is a set of tools and recommendations  it will analyze request patterns and recommend batching, cache policies, and quantization profiles. For example, an LLM chat workload with short prompts will get different suggestions than a long-context summarization job. We'll provide a sandbox so customers can run their prompts and see inferred cost savings before applying changes.

[08:47] Evan Chu: From the runtime side, Optimize will also choose kernels and execution paths when possible so customers get the performance benefit without manually tuning low-level settings.

[09:05] Audience (Q): can Optimize automatically change customer configs or is it advisory?

[09:11] Maya Singh: Initially advisory only  we want to build trust. The roadmap includes an opt-in automated mode for enterprise customers with safety boundaries.

[09:28] Lena Torres: Alright let's go to live Q&A, please raise hands in the chat.

[09:32] [09:32] Speaker: Unlabeled (Engineering)  question about KV cache eviction policies and how they interact with autoscaler.

[09:40] Rajesh Varma: Good question. Current design keeps KV cache warm for in-flight sessions and we tune eviction to favor shorter LRU windows for high-churn workloads. The upcoming predictive scaler will pre-warm nodes based on traffic forecasts to reduce cache misses. There will always be some tradeoff with cost.

[10:12] [10:12] Speaker: Sales: Any updates on enterprise contract length expectations for Dedicated?

[10:18] Kira Moore: Yes, typical is 12 to 36 month commitments depending on reserved capacity. We also offer burst policies for occasional spikes. We'll send a one-pager with recommended contract templates.

[10:41] [10:41] Speaker: Someone in product asks  what telemetry will be available to Private customers for debugging?

[10:50] Evan Chu: Private will include the same per-route latency and token-count dashboard and logs; some SaaS-only features (like global analytics across customers) won't be present of course. We plan to provide a local observability stack and options to forward logs to customer SIEMs.

[11:23] [11:23] Audience: Quick question re: evals  will we keep model evals open-source?

[11:28] Maya Singh: Yes, we'll continue to publish eval harnesses and prompt suites. We believe transparent evals help customers compare model and quantization tradeoffs.

[11:40] [11:40] Speaker: People Ops  any updates on parental leave / comp policies?

[11:44] Ana Gomez: Yes, we're updating the parental leave policy, more details to be posted in HR this week. Also working on comp calibration cycles  managers will receive guidelines by April 20th.

[12:05] [12:05] Lena Torres: We're near the hour mark; quick recap. Q1 was strong, focus for Q2: reliability work (autoscale, kernel selection), product parity for Private, release Optimize beta, close enterprise Dedicated deals. Action items in the meeting notes.

[12:30] [12:30] Lena Torres: Final thoughts  thank you for shipping, for ops work, and for the customer wins. Very proud of what the team's been doing.

[12:48] [12:48] Evan Chu: Small ask  if you have perf regressions or any flaky test that impacts release velocity, file tickets and ping infra. We're prioritizing fixes that block customers.

[13:05] [13:05] Kira Moore: We'll close with a reminder: sales kickoff on April 13th for new pricing & Dedicated packaging docs.

[13:20] [13:20] Lena Torres: Okay that's it. Meeting adjourned. Recording saved; slides and Q&A log in the #all-hands channel.

End transcript.
